title: Why Lester had no imitators: Hawkins, Chu Berry, Ike Quebec
summary: Everyone followed Hawkins and then Chu Berry; Hawkins cut Body and Soul to answer Berry, and Ike Quebec copied that solo.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: I'm still curious to know why it is that Lester didn't have any imitators. Nobody copied Lester. Nobody tried to sound like him.
Well, I knew two or three cats -- I forget their names.
Yeah, around here. They tried to copy Lester. Two or three cats. Then some alto players tried to copy Lester.
I mean, later on, of course, there were plenty of people who copied him.
But I'm talking about at the time.
Nobody in the mid-thirties was trying to play like Lester.
Why was that? Was it because Hawkins was just too big?
Yeah, yeah. All of them were listening to Hawkins. And then Chu Berry come along, and they got behind Chu Berry. That's why Hawkins made that special chorus on "Body and Soul."
To clean up on Chu Berry. He wanted to cut Chu.
Yeah, and he wanted to show all them other boys something.
Yeah. And we had a boy named Ike Quebec. Have you heard Ike Quebec.
Yes, indeed. Yes, he's a good player, too.

Yeah. Well, Ike Quebec had that wrote off. Somebody wrote it off. He had a sheet as long as that whole coffee table there, stretched on his rack. That whole Hawk solo. He played it just like Hawk did. Yeah, he was a devil of a tenor player.
